title: Redeem a gift card inside the transaction

blocks.text: The server now takes gift cards. A redemption is a 0200 with the gift card's number in field 2 and the amount in field 4, and each card's balance is a row in the `gift_cards` table. The chain is `Open`, `Redeem`, a fraud check, `Close` and `SendResponse`, all in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/GiftCards.java`.

`Open`, `Close` and the `debit`, `balance` and `reply` helpers are given. Write `Redeem.prepare`, marked `TODO`. The cashier needs `00` when the card paid, `51` when its balance was too small, and `96` when the database failed. Support has two rules from past incidents: a card whose redemption was declined anywhere in the chain keeps its whole balance, and two lanes redeeming the same card at the same moment never spend more than the card holds. About 15 lines.
The tests deploy a real TransactionManager with Q2 in the test's JVM, in front of a small database that has transactions and row locks.

cases.says: a redemption the balance covers is answered 00 and the amount comes off the card
a redemption larger than the balance is answered 51 and the card keeps its balance
a redemption a later participant declines takes nothing, because the debit went through Open's connection and was rolled back
two redemptions at once can't both spend the same balance, because the check and the debit are one statement in prepare and the row stays locked until Close
a database failure while debiting becomes a 96 answer in prepare, not a transaction nobody answers

origin.section: 9.3 Write in `prepare`, So the Database Can Still Say No

concepts: Open turns auto-commit off and leaves the connection in the Context, participants write through it, and Close commits or rolls back, so a decline anywhere in the chain undoes every write; a write through a connection of its own with auto-commit stays.

A conditional UPDATE in prepare checks and reserves in one statement and holds the row lock until Close, so concurrent requests can't pass the same check and a database failure still becomes a decline; a check in prepare with the write in commit lets both through.
